# Decisions: statusline-refresh

- 2026-08-07T13:59:34.178Z — rule: **statusLine identity is type + command plus the owned-key allowlist — never reintroduce an exact key-count test, and add a key to STATUSLINE_OWN_KEYS only when sofar itself writes it.** — chose **D1: statusline identity is type + command, tolerating exactly one tunable key (refreshInterval), and the installed entry ships refreshInterval: 10. isSofarStatusline matches on type + command and requires every remaining key to be in an owned set {type, command, refreshInterval}; any other extra key (e.g. padding) is still foreign. This recognizes both the legacy two-key entry installed before the key shipped and a user-retuned interval.** over Keeping byte-for-byte identity (Object.keys(v).length === 2) and documenting refreshInterval as a manual edit users make at their own risk; or accepting any object whose command is ours regardless of extra keys. because The two halves were in direct contradiction. refreshInterval is Claude Code's own documented cure for a frozen idle line — the host re-runs a statusLine command only on session start, new assistant message, compact and mode toggles — but under exact-key-count identity, setting it turned sofar's own entry foreign: --uninstall refused to remove it and --install refused to touch it, both telling the user to hand-edit. So the prescribed fix silently broke the uninstall path, reproduced live against 0.23.0. Shipping the key by default removes the discovery burden entirely; widening identity keeps the theirs-wins law intact where it matters (a different command is still someone else's) while an allowlist rather than a blanket accept means an unfamiliar key still counts as customization we must not delete.
